intro: Before you stretches the Aspendos Aqueduct, in Antalya province, from the 2nd century AD. The aqueduct feeding the city crosses its valley on an inverted siphon worked by pressure towers — among the most ambitious pieces of Roman hydraulic engineering.
history: How do you carry water across a valley? Here the answer was an inverted siphon worked by pressure towers. The water drops, then is pushed up the far slope under pressure. This solution avoided the cost of holding an arcade high the whole way, and it ranks among the most ambitious pieces of Roman hydraulic engineering.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the pressure towers, the siphon line, the piers and the header tank.
facts: Did you know? To make the system work, the pressure in the pipes had to be calculated, and exactly how the Romans did that calculation is still not fully known. The line crosses the valley on an inverted siphon worked by pressure towers.
outro: This brings our tour of the Aspendos Aqueduct to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for listening, and enjoy your visit.
